chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who lends another man silver dirhams with interest (ghillah), and he takes from him the 'tazajjiyah' (a type of premium or additional payment). He said, 'There is no harm (in it).' And this was narrated from Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الطَّازَجِيَّةَ: A specific type of premium or additional payment taken by the lender
key_terms.عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a lender to receive an extra payment or premium when lending money with interest in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the permissibility of receiving a non-monetary gift (tazajjiyah) alongside the principal in a loan of silver dirhams, distinguishing it from riba (interest) by avoiding a fixed, contractual increase. The attribution to Imam Ali underscores the continuity of this juristic principle within the Ahl al-Bayt's tradition, while Shaykh al-Tusi’s inclusion in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights its foundational status in Shia fiqh regarding commercial transactions.
